question.:question/problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=\frac{4}{5x}+3?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To plot $y=\frac{4}{5x}+1,$ we apply the following steps:

- Take the curve $y=\frac{1}{x}.$

![](images/a3/a32495fcca947d01cf8d3218fc5cfc0cce083a34e6fb6b629d92ba9e47039a6e.png)

- Then, stretch the result by a scale factor of $\frac{4}{5}$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=\frac{4}{5x}.$

![](images/ea/ea9bd36b532b46d3edcc99497b77e75288499a4b02239f5d2416cff6a4259478.png)

- Translate it by $3$ units up to get the graph of $y=\frac{4}{5x}+3.$

![](images/e6/e6798ba049ab7040eec51d2da525d3383816578423e11384ced1f3665a2e50fd.png)
